task.description: WF-03 Step 3b SECURITY GATE for ISS-0427, dispatched explicitly IN SCOPE despite touching only test/support/ -- the dispatch's own framing is that tenant schema isolation is the mechanism several security invariants rest on, so a clone that is subtly non-equivalent to a migration-built schema degrades the project's security EVIDENCE even with zero production code change. Determine: (1) tenant isolation / no cross-schema leak, (2) the audit_entries/repository_artifacts immutability guarantee survives cloning AND template-drop, (3) the template itself cannot be mistaken for a tenant or reached/reaped/polluted, (4) whether the 13-dimension parity check actually covers security-relevant properties, (5) production path (provision_tenant_schema/1, replay_migrations/2) is genuinely untouched, (6) whether the dormant DOMAIN/ENUM/collation residual (OQ-6) is safely deferrable. Name applicable invariants with severity; do not wave this through as 'just tests.'

result.summary:
SCOPE TEST applied per .claude/agents/security-reviewer.md's five conditions against the real diff (git diff main...HEAD --stat, git diff main...HEAD -- lib/): zero files under lib/ changed except the new design doc (1745 insertions, 0 code). No API route, no priv/repo/migrations/*.exs migration, no secret-resolving code, no response-shaping code, no lookup-by-ID handler. By the LITERAL scope test this is out of scope. I did not stop there, per the dispatch's explicit instruction and per this run's own stated reasoning: tenant schema isolation is the mechanism INV-1 and the audit-immutability guarantee rest on, so a clone that is subtly non-equivalent would make every tenant-isolation test in this suite assert against a weaker artifact while still reporting green -- a degradation of security EVIDENCE, which is exactly what INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) and INV-1's own spirit (schema-per-tenant isolation is checkable, not assumed) exist to catch even when the code creating the evidence lives in test/support/. Treated INV-1 and INV-6 as APPLIES on that basis and ran their verification procedures against the actual mechanism, not the design's account of it.

METHOD: independently re-derived every load-bearing claim rather than inheriting it from the design doc or either ELIXIR-DEV handoff, per core-directives.md's re-derivation rule and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's 'a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong.' Read test/support/tenant_template.ex and the tenant_fixture.ex diff in full. Built my own throwaway probe schemas (probe_tpl/probe_clone) in letflow_dev implementing the exact mechanism test/support/tenant_template.ex uses (LIKE INCLUDING ALL, FK re-add with unquoted qualifier rewrite, sequence recreation, trigger/function re-add with unquoted qualifier rewrite) and ran a single ordered psql session covering insert/update/delete against the clone, then DROP SCHEMA probe_tpl CASCADE, then re-tested the clone. All probe schemas dropped and confirmed absent (SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'probe%' -- 0 rows) before writing this handoff.

1. TENANT ISOLATION -- no cross-schema leak survives. Independently verified all three coupling classes the design names: (a) FK -- pg_get_constraintdef emits the qualifier UNQUOTED (confirmed: 'FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES probe_tpl.parents(id)' with no quote marks), so String.replace(def, 'tenant_template.', clone_schema<>'.') is the correct, non-vacuous rewrite; my probe's clone FK showed 'REFERENCES probe_clone.parents(id)' post-rewrite and rejected an insert with a nonexistent clone-local parent both before AND after the template was dropped. (b) Sequences -- CREATE SEQUENCE probe_clone.parents_id_seq + SET DEFAULT nextval('probe_clone.parents_id_seq') + OWNED BY produced a clone-local sequence; after dropping the template, INSERT into the clone still allocated id=2 correctly (clone's own sequence, no residual pointer to the dropped template's sequence). (c) Triggers/functions -- pg_get_functiondef/pg_get_triggerdef also emit the qualifier UNQUOTED (independently confirmed on my own probe, matching design section 0.5's finding), the rewrite produced a function with a DISTINCT pg_proc OID living in the clone's own namespace, and the trigger's EXECUTE FUNCTION clause pointed at the clone-local function. Confirmed the code (test/support/tenant_template.ex readd_foreign_keys!/1 line 435 and readd_triggers_and_functions!/1 lines 481+489) uses the identical unquoted pattern (~s(#{@template_schema}.), no surrounding quotes) both design and implementation converged on. INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES, PASS -- every cross-schema reference this mechanism creates is rewritten to the clone's own schema before execution, verified structurally (distinct OIDs/namespaces), not just by absence-of-error.

2. IMMUTABILITY GUARANTEE -- confirmed genuinely enforced, not assumed. My own probe (5 real triggers' shape reduced to 2 representative ones: BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE on parents, backed by one plpgsql function that unconditionally RAISEs) reproduced, in one ordered psql session against a real Postgres instance: INSERT into clone succeeds; UPDATE against the clone -> 'ERROR: audit is immutable' (rejected); DELETE against the clone -> 'ERROR: audit is immutable' (rejected); DROP SCHEMA probe_tpl CASCADE (the template, containing zero references back to the clone -- confirmed by the NOTICE listing only probe_tpl's own 3 objects as cascaded, not touching probe_clone); UPDATE against the SAME clone row post-drop -> 'ERROR: audit is immutable' again, byte-identical failure mode, zero residual dependency on the template's continued existence. This independently reproduces ELIXIR-DEV's continuation-handoff claim (section (d) of step-03-elixir-dev-continued.json) rather than inheriting it. Maps to INV-1 (the isolation mechanism the guarantee depends on) and INV-6 (this new data-access path -- clone construction -- proves its scoping via the parity check plus this now-twice-independently-verified functional test) -- both APPLIES, both PASS.

3. THE TEMPLATE ITSELF -- structurally incapable of being mistaken for a tenant, reached by production code, reaped mid-run, or accumulating real tenant data, verified by reading the actual mechanisms rather than trusting the design's claim. (a) Cannot be produced/resolved as a tenant: schema_name_for_tenant/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:166) always emits 'tenant_' <> 32-hex; 'tenant_template' cannot arise from it, and tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (line 195) pattern-matches 'tenant_' <> hex where hex must satisfy ~r/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/ AND be exactly 32 chars -- 'template' (8 chars, contains non-hex letters t/m/p/l) fails both, confirmed by reading the guard directly. (b) No Registration row: Registration.changeset/2 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex:59) calls validate_format(:schema_name, ~r/^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$/) -- verified this regex is real and would reject 'tenant_template' through the normal insert path; the template build (test/support/tenant_template.ex insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/0, lines 254-291) deliberately bypasses this changeset via Repo.insert_all/3 for a TRANSIENT row naming a real throwaway tenant_id, immediately deleted (delete_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1, lines 293-296) before build_template!/0 returns -- confirmed by reading both functions: no Registration row survives naming 'tenant_template'. The clone's own Registration insert (do_clone/2 step 9, lines 396-404) goes through the real Registration.changeset/2 with schema_name: clone_schema (a real tenant_<32hex> value derived from schema_name_for_tenant/1) -- the normal, validated path. (c) Cannot be reaped: read test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex directly -- sweep_orphans/2's candidate query (line 169) is 'SELECT id, tenant_id, schema_name FROM tenant_schemas WHERE provisioned_at < $1', i.e. it selects candidates from the tenant_schemas/Registration table, never by walking pg_namespace directly, and reclaim_row/2 (line 326) only DROPs a schema_name that came from that query. Since (b) establishes no tenant_schemas/Registration row is ever inserted for 'tenant_template', the reaper is structurally incapable of selecting it -- confirmed this is not merely asserted in the design (design section 8 INV-4's own claim) but independently true from reading the reaper's query shape myself. (d) Production code cannot reach it: see item 5 below. (e) Accumulating real tenant data: the template is a test-only Postgres object that never receives INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from application code (no lib/ code path references 'tenant_template' or Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate at all -- confirmed via the lib/ diff being empty and via grep of lib/ finding no reference), and each partition's BEAM VM rebuilds it fresh in its own letflow_test<N> database per design section 4.2 -- 'once per VM' bounded by the VM's own lifetime, not a persistent cross-run artifact. No cleanup-between-runs gap: the database itself is reset between mix test invocations by this repo's existing flow (confirmed by design section 5's own citation of the existing reset flow, and consistent with every other test/support/ fixture's lifecycle assumption in this codebase, e.g. SandboxPool). INV-1: APPLIES, PASS on this dimension too -- the template's own identity is structurally non-tenant-shaped by the same mechanism (schema-name regex) INV-1's isolation model already depends on elsewhere.

4. DOES THE PARITY CHECK PROTECT WHAT SECURITY NEEDS -- yes, on inspection of the actual dimension list (test/support/tenant_template.ex dimension_checks/0, 13 entries) against what carries security weight, not merely 'is it long.' Constraints (dimension 3, includes FK contype='f', compared by pg_get_constraintdef structurally, not by name) and triggers+their backing functions (dimension 8, rewritten this run to a real per-table/per-schema structural comparison after the false 'zero triggers' premise was caught during implementation, per section 0.4 of the design) are exactly the two categories this review's own items 1-2 depend on, and both are checked structurally (definition text, qualifier-normalized) rather than by presence/count alone -- the same discipline that would catch 'FK present but pointing at the template' or 'trigger present but invoking the template's function,' which is the actual failure mode a security reviewer should worry about, not merely 'FK missing.' Sequences (dimension 5) explicitly assert the candidate's own sequence lives IN the candidate's own schema (the direct test for the sequence-trap coupling), NOT NULL/identity (dimension 6) is covered. RLS/tablespace/ownership (dimension 12) are checked and confirmed not-applicable with a stated reason rather than silently skipped -- verified myself that no migration under priv/repo/migrations/ issues ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (grep, zero hits), consistent with the design's own claim. I did not find a security-relevant property (constraint, FK, trigger, NOT NULL, RLS) that the 13 dimensions fail to cover; the two dimensions I most wanted to see (constraints and triggers/functions) are also the two the design's own history shows were caught wrong once and then corrected to genuinely non-vacuous structural checks, with the correction independently reproduced by my own probe in item 1-2 above rather than only claimed. INV-6 (new data-access path proves its scoping): APPLIES, PASS -- the parity check plus a SECURITY-REVIEWER handoff explicitly naming which invariants apply and how they were confirmed (this document) is exactly what INV-6 requires.

5. PRODUCTION PATH UNTOUCHED -- confirmed directly, not assumed. `git diff main...HEAD --stat -- lib/` shows exactly one file: lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md (1745 insertions, a doc, 0 code lines). `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` is empty. Confirmed via direct docker exec against letflow_dev that no tenant_/probe schema exists as residue from this run's own build activity (SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant%' OR nspname LIKE 'probe%' -- 0 rows at review start, 0 rows after my own probes were cleaned up). provision_tenant_schema/1 and replay_migrations/2's bodies are byte-identical to main. The new test/support/ code's only call into lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex is the pre-existing public API (schema_name_for_tenant/1, tenant_scoped_migrations/0, replay_migrations/2 itself called unmodified against a throwaway real tenant) -- read-only usage of functions that already had other test-only callers before this change (TenantFixture). INV-1/INV-6: PASS on this axis -- zero new production-reachable code, so no new tenant-data-path risk surface was introduced in lib/.

6. THE DORMANT RESIDUALS (OQ-6: DOMAIN/ENUM/collation) -- judgement: acceptable to leave to the parity check today, not a BLOCKER, but flagged as a MINOR forward-looking note rather than silently accepted. Independently re-ran the design's own dormancy claim: grep -ril 'CREATE TYPE\|CREATE DOMAIN\|CREATE COLLATION' priv/repo/migrations/*.exs found zero hits (confirmed myself, not inherited) -- there is genuinely no live column in the real tenant schema today whose type or collation resolves outside pg_catalog, so there is no PRESENT security gap to fix. The reasoning for why this is a real (not merely nominal) safety net if a future migration does introduce one: dimension 13's failure mode is a hard, loud ExUnit.AssertionError at template-self-check time (design section 3.4 use site 1) or at the first clone-vs-template test run (use site 2) -- both run every suite invocation per INV-5 (parity is asserted every run, not just once), so a future domain/enum/collation column would fail the FIRST test that provisions any tenant in that partition, not silently degrade. This is a materially different risk posture than a check that only runs occasionally or manually. The severity classification I apply: were this residual to fire today (it cannot, confirmed dormant), the failure mode it protects against (a clone's column type/collation still pointing at the template, which DROP SCHEMA tenant_template CASCADE would cascade-destroy per design section 0.3's own demonstrated hazard) would be an INV-1 BLOCKER if shipped uncaught -- but since it is dormant and the check that would catch it is loud and runs every suite invocation, I am not blocking on OQ-6 as currently written. Recommend (not a gate condition) that OQ-6 be promoted from an open question to a tracked follow-up issue if S3/S4 requirements are expected to introduce a custom DOMAIN/ENUM (e.g. a bounded-value business field) so the mechanism gap is closed before, not after, the parity check's first real failure.

INVARIANT SUMMARY:
- INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES -- PASS. Verified independently via my own probe schema (FK, sequence, trigger/function all correctly clone-scoped and none residually coupled to the template, including after the template is dropped) and via direct reading of schema_name_for_tenant/1, tenant_id_for_schema_name/1, Registration.changeset/2's validate_format regex, and the reaper's query shape.
- INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response type touched, S4 not started.
- INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- S5 not started, no scripting/plugin surface touched.
- INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES (live invariant) -- PASS. `grep -rniE "(password|secret|client_secret|token)\\s*(=|:)\\s*\"[^\"]{8,}\"" test/support/tenant_template.ex test/support/tenant_fixture.ex` found no hits; the module contains no secret material, only schema/table/DDL identifiers and catalog introspection.
- INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint, S4 not started.
- INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES -- PASS. This handoff is that proof: every dimension the parity check covers was checked against what it structurally compares, not merely that it exists; the clone mechanism's own scoping was independently re-derived against live Postgres, not inherited from either ELIXIR-DEV handoff.
- INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): APPLIES (live invariant) -- PASS with note. `grep -rn "Repo.query" test/support/tenant_template.ex` shows every Repo.query!/2 call either uses bind parameters ($1/$2, e.g. template_built_in_db?/0, readd_foreign_keys!/1's discovery query, recreate_sequences!/1's discovery query) OR interpolates identifiers, not data, via ~s(...) string interpolation (schema names, table names, column names, constraint names, and full DDL text read back from Postgres's own pg_get_constraintdef/pg_get_functiondef/pg_get_triggerdef). Confirmed per design section 2.3's own closing paragraph (independently re-verified, not just quoted): every interpolated identifier is either a compile-time-known name from expected_tenant_tables/0 (a fixed, hand-maintained list), the output of schema_name_for_tenant/1 (regex-constrained to tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}), or DDL text read back from Postgres's own catalog functions -- which by construction can only contain names/text Postgres itself already accepted as valid when this codebase's own migrations built the template. None of these five interpolation sites carry caller-supplied or test-input-controlled untrusted string data; this is architecturally the same shape INV-7 already accepts for provision_tenant_schema/1's own existing CREATE SCHEMA <name> pattern, applied to a larger set of DDL-generating call sites. Not a raw-SQL-with-external-input violation.
- INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES (live invariant) -- PASS. `grep -n "^\\s*{:ok, .*} = " test/support/tenant_template.ex` found no bare-match-that-can-raise pattern reachable from external/tenant-controlled input; ensure_template!/0 and clone_tenant_schema!/1 both explicitly raise (ExUnit.AssertionError) or return {:error, {:clone_failed, reason}} on failure per the module's own 'no silent fallback' design (section 5) -- this is deliberate, test-fixture-appropriate fail-loud behavior (an ExUnit test SHOULD fail hard on a broken fixture), not an unhandled crash risk to other tenants' in-flight work, since test/support/ code never runs inside a shared production process.
- INV-9 (SSRF/outbound URL validation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP call in this diff.

No FAIL on any APPLIES invariant. No invariant was skipped by applying the literal scope test alone -- I explicitly overrode the 'zero lib/ diff -> presumptively out of scope' shortcut per the dispatch's own instruction and per my own judgement that this change manufactures the EVIDENCE several tenant-isolation tests rely on, which is squarely what INV-1/INV-6 exist to gate regardless of which directory the gating code lives in.

issues.description: OQ-6 (design section 9): the parity check's dimension 13 (column type/collation namespace) is today a defaults-only, zero-vs-zero rule-out with no corresponding clone-mechanism recreation step, because no tenant-scoped migration currently introduces a custom DOMAIN/ENUM/COLLATION. Independently re-confirmed dormant (grep -ril 'CREATE TYPE\|CREATE DOMAIN\|CREATE COLLATION' priv/repo/migrations/*.exs -- zero hits). This is a real, if currently theoretical, gap: if a future migration introduces one, the clone mechanism has no step to recreate it clone-locally, and dropping the template would cascade-destroy the clone's own columns (design section 0.3's own demonstrated hazard). The parity check WOULD catch this loudly and immediately (every suite run, per INV-5), so this is not a silent-degradation risk today -- but it is a known mechanism gap, not a closed one. Recommend filing a tracked follow-up issue (not a blocker on this run) to close OQ-6's mechanism gap if/when S3/S4 work is expected to introduce a custom DOMAIN, ENUM, or COLLATION on a tenant-scoped table, so the gap closes before the parity check's first real failure rather than after.

result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER (idiom, supervision integrity, scope creep, decision-record consistency) per the standard WF-03 sequence after SECURITY-REVIEWER PASS. No rework required from SECURITY-REVIEWER.
